findings.claim: propose() does not create a feature branch, violating WP-SCP-021 §2 invariant and the dispatch AC
findings.evidence: tools.py:625-668 — propose_impl() calls proposals_root.mkdir() then proposal_path.write_text() directly on the current working tree; no subprocess git-checkout -b or equivalent is executed. branch_name is returned as a string ('scp-mcp-proposal/prop-NNN') but no branch is created. Dispatch AC: 'Writes a new file at docs/reviews/proposals/PROP-NNN.md (auto-incrementing ID) on a feature branch.' WP-SCP-021 §2 invariant: 'Propose() writes only to branches, never to main.'
findings.impact: If scp-mcp-server runs on main or any live branch, proposals write directly to that branch. The isolation invariant is unenforced. A server operator running on main would accumulate proposal files on main itself, which is the exact scenario the §2 invariant prohibits. The 021E adjudication slice depends on this isolation being in place.
findings.mitigation: Before writing the proposal file, execute git checkout -b {branch_name} (or equivalent using gitpython). Return branch_name only after successful branch creation. Add a test that asserts no file is written to the working tree unless a branch was created. If branch creation is intentionally deferred to 021E, the dispatch AC text must be updated to reflect the deferral and the §2 invariant must note the open exception.
